mainTopic: How many full and short months בית דין may set in a year: רב הונא's and עולא's readings of the משנה, each defended against the moon-gap challenge
overview: The משנה says בית דין may not set fewer than four full (30-day) months in a year, and that the חכמים did not want to go beyond eight. רב הונא reads 'eight' as a limit of eight full months. The גמרא challenges him: eight full months would still make the new moon of תשרי appear two days before ראש השנה. It answers with רב משרשיא's case, where the year before was a leap year whose added month was short. That cuts the gap to one day, and people don't pay attention to one day. עולא reads the משנה differently: the limit is eight short (29-day) months, and that is the reason every year needs at least four full months. The גמרא challenges עולא the same way, since eight short months would leave the moon two days late. It answers with the same leap-year case, this time with a full added month, which brings the gap down to one day. People then assume the moon was already seen and that they simply missed it.

steps.title: Eight full months also throw off the moon by two days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רב הונא: if nine full months are banned because the moon would come three days early, eight full months should also be a problem, since the moon would come two days early.
steps.simpleTranslation: With nine full months, the new moon would come three days early! But now too, with eight, it comes two days early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking רב הונא's reading that the משנה limits a year to eight full months. It argues that eight is not much better than nine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real moon-month is about 29½ days, so a balanced year has six full months and six short ones. Every extra full month pushes ראש השנה one day later than the real new moon. Nine full months means three days off, but eight full months still means two days off, so why allow eight?

keyTerms.meaning: the moon
comes early, appears before
now too; even in the allowed case

phrases.english: the moon would come three days early!
phrases.notes: With nine full months, the new moon of תשרי would show up three days before ראש השנה.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי קָא קָדֵים אָתֵי תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי.
phrases.english: Now too, with eight, it comes two days early.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי קָא קָדֵים אָתֵי תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to רב הונא that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that the limit is eight full months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whatever problem rules out nine full months (a three-day gap) also applies to eight (a two-day gap).

steps.title: The year before was a leap year, which cancels one extra day
steps.stepSummary: Using an idea of רב משרשיא, the גמרא explains that the case is one where the previous year had an extra short month. That short month balances one of this year's full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב משרשיא said: for example, when it was a leap year. Here too, the case is when the year before was a leap year, and the added month was a short one. Count one full month against that short month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a specific situation where eight full months do not really create a two-day gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If last year's added leap month had only 29 days, the calendar ran half a day 'short' there. One of this year's full months cancels that out. Then only seven full months actually push the date, which cuts the gap down.

keyTerms.meaning: a leap year, with an extra month added
the added leap month
a full month (30 days)
a short month (29 days)
remove, take away from the count

phrases.english: As Rav Mesharshiyya said,
for example, where it was a leap year,
here too, for example,
where the year before it was a leap year,
and the leap-year addition is a month.
phrases.notes: He means the added month had only 29 days, a short month.

phrases.english: Take away one full month
against the short month.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a year that follows a leap year with a short added month
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eight full months always make the moon two days early.
steps.terutzMaskana: After a leap year with a short added month, one of this year's full months is cancelled out, so only seven count.

steps.title: Even then, one day is still off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: even with only seven full months counting, the moon would still come one day early.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The gap got smaller, but it did not go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven full months is still one more than the balanced six. So the new moon would still appear one day before ראש השנה, and the original worry is not fully solved.

keyTerms.meaning: still, even so

phrases.english: But there is still one day!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Seven full months still leaves a one-day gap between the real new moon and ראש השנה.

steps.title: People don't notice a one-day difference
steps.stepSummary: A one-day gap does not matter, because ordinary people do not pay attention to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: People don't pay attention to that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a one-day difference is too small for people to notice, so it causes no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that people would see the moon out of step with the calendar and mock בית דין. Two or three days is noticeable, but one day is not. So רב הונא's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: people don't pay attention to it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, the limit of eight full months works because, in the right case, it leaves only a one-day gap, and people don't notice one day.

phrases.english: People don't pay attention to it.
phrases.notes: The concern behind all this is that people would see the moon out of step and mock בית דין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 and closes רב הונא's line.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical threshold: a small difference is not noticed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gap at all would cause people to mock בית דין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a gap people notice is a problem, and one day is not noticed.

steps.title: עולא: the limit is eight short months
steps.stepSummary: עולא reads the משנה differently: the חכמים did not allow more than eight short months. That is the reason the משנה requires at least four full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It did not seem right to the חכמים to make more than eight months short. The משנה is giving a reason: Why can't a year have fewer than four full months? Because the חכמים did not want more than eight short months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a second, different reading of the same משנה, from עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the משנה has two limits: at least four full months, and at most eight full months. For עולא, it is one rule plus its reason: at least four full months, because at most eight short months are allowed. Both say the same thing about the minimum, but they differ about the maximum number of full months.

keyTerms.meaning: to make a month short (29 days)
full months (30 days), which get an added day
it is explaining the reason (for the earlier statement)
we do not go below

steps.confusionAlert: The word מְעוּבָּר is used two ways here. 'שנה מעוברת' is a leap year with an extra month, but 'חדשים המעוברים' are full 30-day months that got an extra day. Don't mix them up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new way of reading the משנה. The גמרא will now test עולא's reading with the same kind of challenge it used against רב הונא.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
It did not seem right to the Sages
to make more than eight months short.
And the משנה is saying 'what is the reason':
What is the reason we do not go below
four full months in a year?
Because it did not seem right to the Sages
to make more than eight months short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the משנה from the one רב הונא gave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה forbids more than eight short months, and that is why every year must have at least four full months.

steps.title: Eight short months also leave the moon two days late
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא the same way: nine short months would put the moon three days late, but eight short months still put it two days late.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about nine, that it is not allowed? Because then the moon would be three days late. But now too, with eight, it is two days late!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא's reading with the same argument it used against רב הונא, just in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra short month moves ראש השנה one day earlier than the real new moon. So nine short months make a three-day gap. But eight short months still make a two-day gap, so why is eight allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: what is different about
is extra, lags behind (the moon appears late)
because if so

phrases.english: What is different about nine, that it is not allowed?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן מְיַיתְּרָא סֵיהֲרָא תְּלָתָא יוֹמֵי,
phrases.english: Because if so, the moon would be three days late.
phrases.notes: Here the new moon of תשרי would show up three days after ראש השנה, not before it.

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי קָא מְיַיתְּרָא תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי!
phrases.english: But now too, it is two days late!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reading from step 5, the same way step 1 challenged רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reading that the limit is eight short months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Whatever problem rules out nine short months (a three-day lag) also applies to eight (a two-day lag).

steps.title: Applying רב משרשיא's leap-year idea to עולא's version
steps.stepSummary: To defend עולא, the גמרא again uses רב משרשיא's case: the year before was a leap year, so its extra full month cancels out one of this year's short months.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב משרשיא said in another place, the case is one where the year was a leap year. Here too, the case is where the year before was a leap year. Take away one short month, since it is balanced by the extra full month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge to עולא from step 6 by reusing the answer it gave earlier: picture a case where last year was a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Last year's added month was a full month, which balances out one of this year's eight short months. So only seven short months really push the calendar against the moon, and the gap shrinks from two days to one. The גמרא repeats the step 2 answer almost word for word, but with the months reversed: a short month is taken away against a full one.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too, the same idea applies to this case

steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a copy of step 2. The גמרא is repeating the same words on purpose, now to answer the challenge against עולא.

phrases.english: As Rav Mesharshiyya said,
for example, where the year was a leap year,
here too
the case is where the year before it was a leap year,
so take away one short month
against the extra full month.
phrases.notes: The extra full month is the month that was added to last year's leap year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 6 challenge against עולא by reusing the step 2 answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the year before was a leap year
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Eight short months would always put the moon two days off, so עולא's limit makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: When last year had an extra full month, one short month is cancelled, so only seven count.

steps.title: There is still a one-day gap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even with only seven short months counting, the moon would still be one day off.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is still one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. Even after removing one short month, a one-day difference is left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seven short months still leave the calendar one day apart from the real new moon. If people notice that, they could still mock the בית דין, so the answer seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: One day

phrases.english: But there is still one day,
phrases.notes: He means a one-day gap between ראש השנה and when the new moon is actually seen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leap-year answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The leap-year answer given in defense of עולא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Removing one short month still leaves a one-day gap, so the problem has not fully gone away.

steps.title: People ignore a one-day gap
steps.stepSummary: A one-day gap is no problem: people assume the moon was seen a day earlier and that they just did not notice it.
steps.simpleTranslation: People assume: it really was seen, and we just did not pay attention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a one-day difference does not cause embarrassment, because people blame themselves for missing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a gap of two days or more would make people think the בית דין made a mistake. With one day, people figure witnesses saw the moon and they personally missed it. This saves עולא's reading that the חכמים allowed at most eight short months.

keyTerms.meaning: They assume, they think
It was indeed seen (the doubled verb adds emphasis)
We did not pay attention, it was not on our minds

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the leap-year case brings the gap down to one day, and a one-day gap causes no trouble. For רב הונא (moon one day early), people simply don't pay attention. For עולא (moon one day late), people assume the moon was seen a day earlier and they just missed it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the defense of עולא's reading, using the same steps as the first version.

phrases.english: They assume:
it really was seen,
phrases.notes: The new moon was seen by witnesses the day before.

phrases.english: and we just did not pay attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבְרִי: אִיתְחֲזוֹיֵי אִיתְחֲזִי וַאֲנַן לָאו אַדַּעְתִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 8 objection about the remaining one day.
steps.terutzResolutionType: How people actually react: a small gap goes unnoticed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any gap at all would make people mock the בית דין.
steps.terutzMaskana: A one-day gap is put down to people's own carelessness, so it causes no problem.
